COMM 100.title: Introduction to Business
COMM 100.description: An overview of all functional areas of business. Students will be introduced to the computer and internet tools commonly used in business. For non-Commerce students only.

COMM 101.title: Business Fundamentals
COMM 101.description: The different disciplines of business and their combination in management planning and decision-making.

COMM 105.title: Values, Ethics, and Community
COMM 105.description: An introduction to the roles and responsibilities of business at individual, organizational, and societal levels. Students will examine their personal values and lay the foundation for ongoing, active exploration of career paths through which they can achieve their goals.

COMM 120.title: Business Immersion
COMM 120.description: A broad introduction to the field of business and how the different disciplines within business interact and combine in business decision-making. For Master of Management - Dual Degree Option students only.

COMM 190.title: Introduction to Quantitative Decision Making
COMM 190.description: Introduction to decision models in business, including basic optimization, linear programming, probability, decision analysis, random variables, simulation, and solving decision problems using spreadsheet tools. Strongly recommended as corequisite: One of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184.

COMM 191.title: Application of Statistics in Business
COMM 191.description: Methods and applications of statistics in business; data analysis, descriptive regression; data generation; sampling distributions; hypothesis testing; confidence intervals; two sample problems; inference in regression.

COMM 192.title: Management and Organizational Behaviour
COMM 192.description: Behaviour in organizations as it affects people as individuals, their relationships with others, their performance in groups and their effectiveness at work.

COMM 196.title: Business Communications I
COMM 196.description: An activity-focused course providing the opportunity to study and practice forms of written and non-written communication needed in business.

COMM 201.title: Study Abroad, Non-Commerce
COMM 201.description: A study abroad program developed in cooperation between UBC Faculty of Commerce and another institution offering a set of courses tailored to a particular field of study.

COMM 202.title: Career Fundamentals
COMM 202.description: Fundamentals of career management including effective resume and cover letter writing, performing well in interviews and learning about the recruiting cycles, networking and resources available at the Hari B. Varshney Business Career Centre.

COMM 203.title: Managing the Employment Relationship
COMM 203.description: The role of employment relations in enterprise performance. Managing employees under statutory law, collective bargaining, and progressive human resource management. Key issues in forming, developing, and maintaining a work force.
COMM 203.prerequisiteText: One of COMM_V 192, COMM_V 292, MGMT_O 230 and either (a) all of ECON_V 101 or ECON_O 101 and ECON_V 102 or ECON_O 102 or (b) ECON_V 100

COMM 204.title: Logistics and Operations Management
COMM 204.description: The design and management of systems to make products, provide services and deliver them to the end user.
COMM 204.prerequisiteText: One of COMM_V 190, COMM_V 290 and one of COMM_V 191, COMM_V 291, STAT_V 200, STAT_O 205, STAT_O 124, STAT_O 230

COMM 205.title: Introduction to Management Information Systems
COMM 205.description: Overview of computer technology and terminology; use of computers as managerial and administrative tools; the management of computer resources and the influence of information technology within the organization.

COMM 220.title: Business Communications
COMM 220.description: An experiential course covering a broad range of business writing and communications. For Master of Management - Dual Degree Option students only.

COMM 271.title: Introduction to Capital Markets
COMM 271.description: Roles of capital market institutions and participants. Skill development for basic financial principles in the quantitative and qualitative evaluation of bond and stock investments.

COMM 280.title: Entrepreneurship
COMM 280.description: Entrepreneurial essentials from creating viable opportunities through building a founding team, strategic planning, going to market, fleshing out an organization and planning the future of the business.

COMM 293.title: Financial Accounting
COMM 293.description: Introduction to the construction and interpretation of financial reports prepared primarily for external use.
COMM 293.prerequisiteText: One of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184, MATH_O 100, MATH_O 116

COMM 294.title: Managerial Accounting
COMM 294.description: Introduction to the development and use of accounting information for management planning and control and the development of cost information for financial reports.

COMM 295.title: Managerial Economics
COMM 295.description: Economic foundations of managerial decision-making. Demand theory, cost and production, market structure, competitive strategy, organization of the firm, welfare-economic foundations of business regulation.
COMM 295.prerequisiteText: Either (a) ECON_V 100 or (b) all of ECON_V 101 or ECON_O 101, ECON_V 102 or ECON_O 102

COMM 296.title: Introduction to Marketing
COMM 296.description: Basic considerations affecting the domestic and international marketing of goods and services.
COMM 296.corequisiteText: COMM_V 293 and one of COMM_V 295, ECON_V 201, ECON_V 301

COMM 298.title: Introduction to Finance
COMM 298.description: Introduces the basic principles of financial valuation, including the time-value of money and the risk/return tradeoff. Develops tools for the quantitative analysis of corporate and/or individual financing and saving decisions, and of capital budgeting decisions.
COMM 298.corequisiteText: COMM_V 293 and one of COMM_V 190, COMM_V 290

COMM 300.title: Study Abroad, Commerce
COMM 300.description: A study abroad program developed in cooperation between UBC Faculty of Commerce and another institution offering a set of courses tailored to a particular field of study.

COMM 301.title: Study Abroad, Commerce
COMM 301.description: A study abroad program developed in cooperation between the Sauder School of Business and another institution offering a set of courses tailored to a particular field of study. Pass/Fail.

COMM 302.title: Study Abroad, Non-Commerce
COMM 302.description: A study abroad program developed in cooperation between UBC Faculty of Commerce and another institution offering a set of courses tailored to a particular field of study.

COMM 303.title: Study Abroad, Non-Commerce
COMM 303.description: A study abroad program developed in cooperation between the Sauder School of Business and another institution offering a set of courses tailored to a particular field of study. Pass/Fail.

COMM 306.title: Urban Land Economics
COMM 306.description: Examines economic factors affecting the urban land market, with an emphasis on determinants of urban land values, the housing market, urban transportation, and land use policies.

COMM 307.title: Real Estate Investment
COMM 307.description: Evaluation of investment in real estate assets; proforma analysis, property and asset management, equity securitization, appraisal, and international real estate investment.
COMM 307.prerequisiteText: One of COMM_V 295, ECON_V 201, ECON_V 301 and COMM_V 298

COMM 310.title: Simulation Models in Business Decision-Making
COMM 310.description: Computer simulation, simulation languages. Typical business applications in financial planning, waiting line problems and other operating problems.

COMM 312.title: Business Ethics Leadership
COMM 312.description: Skill Development for leading organizations while better managing for values. Recognizing organizational values, and developing concrete plans for better delivering on these values.

COMM 314.title: Strategies for Responsible Business
COMM 314.description: Tools to apply sustainable and responsible decision making through individual, organizational, and structural lenses. Topics include diversity and group think, the circular economy, and climate change adaptation.

COMM 320.title: Foundations in Accounting I
COMM 320.description: Preparation of financial statements and use of financial information contained in financial statements to make better decisions. For Master of Management - Dual Degree Option students only.

COMM 321.title: Organizational Behaviour
COMM 321.description: Effects of individual and group behaviour on organizational processes and outcomes. Application of relevant frameworks from the social sciences to particular organizational situations. For Master of Management - Dual Degree Option students only.

COMM 323.title: Leading Diversity, Equity and Inclusion in Organizations
COMM 323.description: Topics in diversity related to identity, group categorization, stereotyping, explicit and implicit bias, microaggressions, and discrimination. Mitigation of institutional inequality and discrimination through inclusive leadership and critical analysis of organizational practices and policies.

COMM 324.title: People Analytics
COMM 324.description: Application of descriptive and inferential statistics to decisions in core Human Resources (HR) areas, including recruitment, selection, compensation, training, and performance management using organizations. HR data and human capital metrics. Machine learning and AI in strategic HR decision making.
COMM 324.prerequisiteText: All of COMM_V 191 or STAT_V 200, COMM_V 203, COMM_V 205

COMM 335.title: Information Systems Technology and Development
COMM 335.description: Introduction to information technology related to business use. Design, implementation and application of Information Systems.

COMM 336.title: Introduction to Digital Business
COMM 336.description: Business fundamentals in the digital economy: leveraging digitization and automation; data and analytics; platforms; crowdsourcing; understanding the impact of digital technologies on firms, markets, economies as well as individuals and society.

COMM 337.title: Business Programming and Analytics
COMM 337.description: Introduction to object-oriented computer programming; computational thinking; program design; scripting; documentation techniques; file handling; database access; and web crawling techniques. Students will apply data structures and programming constructs to the development of business analytics and other related applications.

COMM 338.title: Management of Cybersecurity
COMM 338.description: Fundamentals of cybersecurity from managerial perspectives; Cyber risk management and governance; Security architecture and design; Capabilities to protect enterprise assets and respond to cyber incidents.

COMM 340.title: Service Operations
COMM 340.description: This primarily case-based course will cover service operations in general (50%), health care operations (25%), and revenue management (25%). Applications of queuing models will be included in both services in general and healthcare.

COMM 341.title: Supply Chain Management
COMM 341.description: Integrated management of production and logistics systems; management of inter-organizational relationships in the supply chain, including vendor selection, bidding and negotiation processes, partnering and performance measurement.

COMM 342.title: Global Supply Chain & Logistics Management I - Study Abroad

COMM 343.title: Global Supply Chain & Logistics Management II - Study Abroad

COMM 344.title: Global Supply Chain & Logistics Management III - Study Abroad

COMM 345.title: Global Supply Chain & Logistics Management IV - Study Abroad

COMM 349.title: Logistics Services Management
COMM 349.description: Overview of the characteristics and commercial environment of logistics and transportation services; service operations planning and design, costing, pricing and quality management.

COMM 353.title: Financial Accounting: Intermediate I
COMM 353.description: An examination of accounting as a means of measurement and as an information system for external reporting purposes.

COMM 354.title: Cost Accounting
COMM 354.description: The provision and analysis of cost accounting information that will assist management in making operating decisions and in evaluating operational performance. The utilization of statistical analysis and linear models is included.
COMM 354.prerequisiteText: All of COMM_V 293, COMM_V 294 and one of COMM_V 190, COMM_V 290 and one of COMM_V 191, COMM_ 291, STAT_V 200

COMM 355.title: Income Taxation
COMM 355.description: A study of income tax from the standpoint of the individual and of business enterprise.

COMM 362.title: Consumer Behaviour
COMM 362.description: The use of consumer research and theory in marketing and policy decisions. Psychological, sociological and economic theory and research relevant to consumer behaviour are considered.

COMM 363.title: Marketing Analysis
COMM 363.description: Analytical methods applicable to marketing management decision making; attention to strategic considerations linking analysis of consumer data, corporate data, environmental factors, and competitive response. The course makes extensive use of strategy simulations.

COMM 365.title: Market Research
COMM 365.description: The process of marketing research including topics such as problem/opportunity formulation, research objectives, data sources, research instrument design, sampling, data collection and processing and methods of data analysis.
COMM 365.prerequisiteText: COMM_V 296 and one of COMM_V 190, COMM_V 290 and one of COMM_V 191, COMM_V 291, STAT_V 200 and one of COMM_V 295, ECON_V 201, ECON_V 301

COMM 370.title: Corporate Finance
COMM 370.description: Examination of corporate enterprise decisions including capital budgeting; capital structure choice, and financial policies, tools, and valuation.

COMM 371.title: Investment Theory
COMM 371.description: Basic concepts of finance, including security valuation, security markets, and financial decisions concerning risk and return.

COMM 374.title: Applied Financial Markets
COMM 374.description: Introduction to methodologies and evidence concerning the structure and operation of security markets and the valuation of financial securities including stocks, bonds, options and futures contracts; portfolio management, corporate finance and investment decisions.

COMM 375.title: Behavioural Finance
COMM 375.description: The psychological processes that give rise to decision-making biases in investment settings and counter-strategies to minimize their negative effects on financial decisions.

COMM 376.title: Financial Institutions I
COMM 376.description: The roles and operation of financial institutions, including banks, and the financial systems and markets in which they function, including those involving payments processes and the creation and use of fiat and digital money including cryptocurrencies.

COMM 377.title: International Financial Markets and Institutions
COMM 377.description: Structure, nature and institutions of foreign exchange markets, including spot, forward, futures, options, and offshore currency markets. Factors affecting exchange rates are also discussed.

COMM 379.title: Introduction to Pensions and Insurance
COMM 379.description: Financial dimensions and institutional structure of the pension and insurance industry; calculation of annuities and other aspects of actuarial science based on probability distributions and asset returns. Suitable for students in mathematics who have taken basic finance and for commerce students in finance, accounting and related areas.

COMM 380.title: Co-operative Work Placement I
COMM 380.description: Approved and supervised work experience for a minimum of 3.5 months. Normally taken during the winter term of the third year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Commerce. Option-specific prerequisites apply.

COMM 381.title: Co-operative Work Placement II
COMM 381.description: Approved and supervised work experience for a minimum of 3.5 months. Normally taken during the summer term of the third year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Commerce.

COMM 382.title: Economics of Entrepreneurship and Innovation
COMM 382.description: Fundamental economic issues faced by entrepreneurs who want to commercialize innovations within start-ups and established firms.

COMM 383.title: Innovation Leadership
COMM 383.description: Social science frameworks useful for understanding organizational innovation processes and application of these frameworks to innovation. Diagnosing and solving a broad range of organizational innovation challenges from the perspective of an innovation leader.

COMM 387.title: Entrepreneurial Finance and Private Equity
COMM 387.description: Financial issues encountered by entrepreneurs and those active on the investing side of entrepreneurship, such as working for banks, venture capital firms, or corporate venture organizations, or anyone interacting with entrepreneurs and private equity investors.

COMM 388.title: Design Methods for Business Innovation
COMM 388.description: Studio-based experience in thinking strategies and design processes applied to business innovation in the private, public, and social sectors. Emphasis on problem solving, co-creation, and innovation for external clients in a collaborative environment.

COMM 389.title: Creativity in Business
COMM 389.description: The role and importance of creativity in developing successful business solutions.

COMM 393.title: Commercial Law
COMM 393.description: Introduction to the law of contracts, with particular reference to contracts for sale of goods and related law of personal property; principles of agency, partnerships and company law.

COMM 394.title: Environment, Society, and Government
COMM 394.description: Roles of government and business in the Canadian economy, emphasizing interactions with the environment and society, including Indigenous communities. Ethical foundations of government, business and personal decision-making.

COMM 395.title: Business Communications
COMM 395.description: Understanding non-written communications in day-to-day business.

COMM 396.title: Business Communications II
COMM 396.description: An activity-focused course providing the opportunity to study and practice forms of written communication needed in business.

COMM 405.title: Real Estate Finance
COMM 405.description: The role of mortgage markets, mathematical analysis of return and valuation issue and methods of dealing with lender and borrower risk exposure.

COMM 407.title: Real Estate Economics
COMM 407.description: The economics of real estate markets. Topics include real estate cycles and bubbles, search models and vacancy, the relationship between real estate and the economy, housing demand, and models of housing supply.

COMM 408.title: Real Estate Development
COMM 408.description: The development process from theories of development, market analysis, site selection, project design, land use regulation and financial analysis.

COMM 411.title: Intermediate Business Statistics
COMM 411.description: Statistical techniques useful in business environments. Includes regression analysis, analysis of variance, forecasting, and logit and probit analysis. Credit may be obtained for only one of STAT_V 300, STAT_V 306, and COMM_V 411.

COMM 412.title: Negotiation
COMM 412.description: Negotiation simulations to provide experience and confidence in the negotiation process and to develop effective skills for achieving objectives.

COMM 414.title: Data Visualization and Business Analytics
COMM 414.description: Descriptive analytics including data analysis and visualization. Predictive analytics including forecasting and various statistical techniques. Predictive analytics including optimization, Monte Carlo simulation, decision trees, and discrete event simulation.

COMM 415.title: Operations and Climate
COMM 415.description: Quantitative and qualitative evaluation of public policies and corporate strategies using statistical evaluation methods, cost benefit analysis, and other modelling tools, with a focus on the impacts of climate change on operations and vice versa. Industries including service provision, manufacturing, and infrastructure investment are assessed based on pricing, operating costs, emissions, and other environmental and societal impacts.

COMM 420.title: Marketing
COMM 420.description: Basic considerations affecting the domestic and international marketing of goods and services. Analytical frameworks and techniques that are used to guide marketing strategy decisions. For Master of Management - Dual Degree Option students only.

COMM 421.title: Introductory Finance
COMM 421.description: Introduces the basic principles of financial valuation, including the time-value of money and the risk/return tradeoff. Develops tools for the quantitative analysis of corporate and/or individual financing and saving decisions, and of capital budgeting decisions. For Master of Management - Dual Degree Option students only.

COMM 425.title: Research Methods for Human Resource Management
COMM 425.description: Techniques for collection and analysis of data in organizations to support adoption and administration of human resource management.
COMM 425.prerequisiteText: COMM_V 327 and one of COMM_V 191, COMM_V 291, STAT_V 200 and one of COMM_V 192, COMM_V 292

COMM 428.title: Selected Topics in Human Resource Management

COMM 431.title: Law of Business Organizations and Corporate Governance
COMM 431.description: Statutory provisions and case law that regulate the creation and governance of sole proprietorships, partnerships, corporations, joint ventures, and franchises in British Columbia. Fiduciary duties of partners, directors and officers are also examined.

COMM 434.title: Land Law
COMM 434.description: Legal principles and concepts relating to real estate and land development.

COMM 435.title: CIO Strategies
COMM 435.description: Common issues faced by Chief Information Officers (CIO): Cost and value of information technology (IT), IT priorities, IT and the Board of Directors, Business-IT alignment, IT governance, IT talent management, standardization vs. innovation, project and vendor management/partnering, and managing security and risks.

COMM 436.title: Information Systems Analysis and Design
COMM 436.description: The process of information systems development; modern techniques and tools for systems analysis and design.

COMM 437.title: Database Technology
COMM 437.description: Theory and technology of database management from an applications perspective; database design; database administration.

COMM 438.title: Management of Information Systems
COMM 438.description: Managerial issues in the administration of computerized information systems.

COMM 439.title: Business Data Communications
COMM 439.description: Basic data communications concepts and technology; local area, wide area, and enterprise networks; the Internet; wireless networking; network development life cycle; network security and management.

COMM 441.title: Advanced Business Logistics
COMM 441.description: Analysis of logistics systems within firms and across supply chains. The formulation of corporate logistics strategies.

COMM 444.title: Air Transportation
COMM 444.description: An integrative treatment of air transport management including: demand analysis, sales and marketing, globalization trends, aircraft selection and fleet planning; airport economics and management.

COMM 445.title: Maritime and International Transportation
COMM 445.description: The characteristics of shipping services and the role of shipping services in the design and management of international logistics systems.

COMM 446.title: Transportation Economics
COMM 446.description: Economic characteristics of passenger and freight transportation services; market structure of the transportation industry; economic impact of public regulation and promotion and the role of economic analysis in resolving problems of Canadian policy.
COMM 446.prerequisiteText: One of COMM_V 295, ECON_V 201, ECON_V 301, ECON_V 206

COMM 447.title: Applied Project Management
COMM 447.description: Project management methodology based on the practices defined by the Project Management Institute, including planning, execution, monitoring, control, and completion.

COMM 448.title: Business Logistics and Logistics Services Management
COMM 448.description: General services management including warehousing, transportation, intermodal, order-fulfillment, dispatching, and more.

COMM 450.title: Financial Accounting - Intermediate II
COMM 450.description: Intermediate II. Continuation of the examination of accounting as a means of measurement and as an information system for external reporting purposes.

COMM 451.title: Climate-Focused ESG Reporting and Analysis
COMM 451.description: Analysis of organizations' sustainability reports and climate disclosures through key sustainability reporting concepts, frameworks, and standards as they evolve. The course includes practical application of concepts through real-world examples and cases of ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) reporting.

COMM 452.title: Taxes and Decision Making
COMM 452.description: Analysis of business and financial decisions in the presence of taxes.

COMM 453.title: Financial Accounting-Advanced
COMM 453.description: An examination of advanced financial accounting.

COMM 454.title: Accounting for Management Control and Incentives
COMM 454.description: Design of accounting systems for facilitating and influencing management decisions, with emphasis on performance evaluation in organizations.

COMM 455.title: Principles of Auditing
COMM 455.description: Principles of internal control, audit evidence, sampling and testing; audit reports; standards; responsibilities of the external auditor.

COMM 456.title: Information Technology Risks, Protection and Audit
COMM 456.description: Business risks associated with the use of information technology. Controls for integrity, security safety, and privacy of hardware, software, data and communications. Methods for auditing information systems and their controls.

COMM 459.title: Financial Statement Analysis
COMM 459.description: An examination of financial statement information from the perspective of decision makers external to the firm, e.g., investors and financial institutions.

COMM 460.title: Social and Nonprofit Marketing
COMM 460.description: Examines the role, use, and application of marketing in government agencies and nonprofit institutions.

COMM 461.title: Business Development
COMM 461.description: Principles and practice of personal selling and leadership of teams: strategy, tactics, and implementation.

COMM 462.title: Integrated Marketing Communication
COMM 462.description: Marketing communication campaign strategy, conceptual framework, and practical application for integrated marketing communications, including advertising.

COMM 463.title: Public Relations
COMM 463.description: Managing an organization's strategic communications and relationships with diverse publics to handle issues, strengthen reputation, fulfill social responsibilities, and build trust. Topics include stakeholder engagement, issues management, crisis communications, and events and sponsorship.

COMM 464.title: Digital Marketing
COMM 464.description: Investigation of Internet-based marketing, emphasizing customer-focused perspectives, competitive situations and analysis of the effectiveness of business websites using marketing principles and practices.

COMM 466.title: New Venture Design
COMM 466.description: Teams comprising students in COMM_V 466 and APSC_V 486 propose a new product, produce a viable prototype, and develop a business plan for the marketplace.

COMM 467.title: Brand Management
COMM 467.description: Issues and challenges commonly faced by brand managers, including: assessing brand meaning, evaluating brand health, assessing a brand's leverage potential, evaluating brand extensions, managing brands through a crisis, and assessing brand value.

COMM 468.title: Marketing Applications
COMM 468.description: A capstone marketing course where student teams develop comprehensive marketing plans for corporate clients by conducting industry analyses and crafting creative marketing strategies.

COMM 469.title: International Marketing
COMM 469.description: An analysis of the scope and significance of contemporary international business operations with particular reference to the marketing management problems encountered by firms with multinational branches and subsidiaries.

COMM 470.title: Venture Capital
COMM 470.description: Theory and evidence concerning venture capital markets. Contracting, fundraising, and financing choice covered in depth, with the aim of catering to students looking to raise money for entrepreneurial ventures or to invest in entrepreneurial ventures.

COMM 471.title: Mergers and Acquisitions
COMM 471.description: Mergers and acquisitions as a focal point in making important corporate decisions deduced from careful study of relevant business cases.

COMM 474.title: Fixed Income Markets and Management
COMM 474.description: Fixed income instruments and derivatives. Risk profiles and their use in establishing fixed income investment portfolios. Performance attribution techniques.

COMM 475.title: Investment Policy
COMM 475.description: The management of security portfolios for individual and institutional investors; relation of investment policy to money markets and business fluctuations.

COMM 476.title: Advanced Topics in Investment Management
COMM 476.description: Applications of contemporary research, innovations, and technologies in the allocation of capital across asset classes, portfolios of assets, and individual securities. Empirical analyses of current market data using software and quantitative tools to implement potential investment and trading strategies.

COMM 477.title: Risk Management and Financial Engineering
COMM 477.description: Principles of financial engineering and risk management. Use of derivatives in risk management. Valuation and hedging models for contingent claims.

COMM 479.title: Advanced Topics on Corporate Finance
COMM 479.description: Corporate Finance is the process by which corporations raise money, allocate funds to real assets, and manage the flow of funds back to the investors. Topics will vary according to interests of students, instructors, and developments in the field.

COMM 480.title: Co-operative Work Placement III
COMM 480.description: Approved and supervised work experience for a minimum of 3.5 months. Normally taken during the summer term of the fourth year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative. Education Program in Commerce.

COMM 481.title: Co-operative Work Placement IV
COMM 481.description: Approved and supervised work experience for a minimum of 3.5 months. Normally taken during the fall term of the fourth year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Commerce.

COMM 482.title: New Product Development
COMM 482.description: How new products are developed and the factors that influence success and failure throughout the various stages of development.

COMM 483.title: Leadership and General Management
COMM 483.description: Integration and application of business knowledge to make business decisions across disciplines; development of personal leadership ability and style. Case-based with guest speakers.

COMM 484.title: Sustainability Marketing
COMM 484.description: Role of marketing in creating social value. Integration of marketing fundamentals with core social, environmental, and economic principles of sustainability. Analysis of current sustainability trends. Development of strategic and practical marketing recommendations for for-profit enterprises. Potential and pitfalls of sustainability marketing.

COMM 485.title: Social Entrepreneurship
COMM 485.description: An applied course that examines the innovative, growing, and rapidly evolving field of social entrepreneurship, which tackles social and environmental challenges through business perspectives and methods.

COMM 487.title: Environmental Management
COMM 487.description: Explores corporate environmental strategy by introducing economic principles underlying environmental policy, law, and technologies for pollution prevention and abatement, environmental management systems, ISO-14001, energy systems, eco-marketing, and life-cycle analysis.

COMM 488.title: Public Sector Management
COMM 488.description: This course focuses on some of the distinctive aspects of managing in the public sector.

COMM 489.title: Investing in CDL Start-ups
COMM 489.description: Students work with the Creative Destruction Lab team to support science and technology start-ups through market, customer, and financial analysis. Students learn how investors assess opportunities through due diligence, valuation, and investment memos, gaining direct experience with early-stage investment decisions.

COMM 490.title: Directed Studies in Commerce
COMM 490.description: An investigation and report on a topic to be agreed upon by a member of the faculty and a senior student.

COMM 491.title: Strategic Management
COMM 491.description: Concepts and processes for the strategic management of private sector, single and multi-business unit enterprises are analysed using the case method. Methodologies which draw on economic and organizational theory are integrated to form the foundations for strategic analyses.
COMM 491.prerequisiteText: Fourth-year standing. Either (a) all of COMM_V 390, COMM_V 395 or (b) COMM_V 396

COMM 492.title: Management Simulation
COMM 492.description: Student teams manage hypothetical firms in a complex simulation, coordinating production, finance, marketing and strategic planning in competition with other teams.
COMM 492.prerequisiteText: Fourth-year standing. Either (a) COMM_V 390, COMM_V 395 or (b) COMM_V 396

COMM 495.title: Business and Sustainable Development
COMM 495.description: An overview of environmental issues, focusing on corporate strategy, government policy and interactions between these two sectors of the economy.

COMM 497.title: New Enterprise Development
COMM 497.description: The particular problems and experiences encountered in starting, developing and managing new enterprises. The course includes lectures, guest speakers, and case studies.
COMM 497.prerequisiteText: Fourth-year standing. Either (a) all of COMM_V 390, COMM_V 395 or (b) COMM_V 396

COMM 498.title: International Business Management
COMM 498.description: Development of general environmental framework for international business studies by drawing on international and development economics, research into government-business relations and studies in comparative socio-cultural systems and political systems.
COMM 498.prerequisiteText: Either (a) all of COMM_V 390, COMM_V 395 or (b) COMM_V 396

COMM 525.title: Introduction to Behavioural Research Methods for Business

COMM 528.title: Advanced Topics in Human Resource Management

COMM 583.title: Forecasting and Time Series Analysis in Business Environments

COMM 611.title: Seminar on Theoretical Developments in Management

COMM 622.title: Seminar in Classics and Theory Construction in Organizational Behaviour

COMM 623.title: Qualitative Research Methods in Organizational Behaviour

COMM 633.title: Modelling Methods in the Research and Practice of Information Systems

prerequisite.raw: At least nine graduate course credits in information system topics

COMM 633.prerequisiteText: At least nine graduate course credits in information system topics

COMM 634.title: Empirical Research Methods in Information Systems

COMM 635.title: Advanced Topics in Management Information Systems

COMM 651.title: Analysis of Accounting Information in Markets

COMM 654.title: Analysis of Accounting Information in Organizations

COMM 659.title: Advanced Topics in Empirical Accounting Research

COMM 661.title: Analytical Methods and Models in Marketing

COMM 672.title: Advanced Topics in Theoretical Corporate Finance

COMM 673.title: Advanced Topics in Theoretical Asset Pricing

COMM 674.title: Advanced Topics in Empirical Asset Pricing

COMM 676.title: Advanced Topics in Empirical Corporate Finance

COMM 691.title: Advanced Topics in Strategy and Business Economics

COMM 692.title: Research Seminar in Strategy and Business Economics

COMM 694.title: Advanced Topics in Urban Land Economics

COMM 696.title: Applied Research in Business Economics and Strategy
